subtype: Stage 7: Confidence and a new edge [Actor]
passage:
Alka, you ask why your Bhupen Mama still gets up at six to go to the workshop. Listen. At twenty-five I made my first dovetail drawer that closed with a soft puff of air, no gaps, no glue showing. Old Mistry-ji tapped it and said, 'Hm. Not bad.' From him that was a medal. I carried that drawer home on the bus on my lap like a baby.
And you know what I felt the next morning? Hungry. I wanted to try a curved front, a hidden joint, a whole cabinet. I also looked at Mistry-ji's joints again and saw a hundred small things mine didn't have yet. It humbled me, but it didn't frighten me.
Two years of split wood had taught me one thing: the stuck months go somewhere. So I went back to the bench.

qa.q: What did Mistry-ji say when he tapped Bhupen's drawer?
How did Bhupen feel the morning after making the drawer, and what shows it?
qa.a: He felt proud and hungry for more, which shows in wanting to try a curved front, a hidden joint and a whole cabinet.

qa.q: What does Bhupen's attitude teach about what to do after a success?
qa.a: It shows you can enjoy the pride, then look honestly at what still remains to learn and go back to steady practice without fear.

qa.q: How might Alka see her Mama's six o'clock habit after hearing the story?
qa.a: She may understand it as trust built from past struggle, not just strictness, and see that the stuck months led somewhere real.

grounding: It shows success bringing pride and a hunger for the next level along with fresh humility, and trust that struggle leads somewhere.

subtype: Stage 7: Confidence and a new edge [Actor]
passage:
The rain started as Pema turned off the main road at Ghoom, a thick grey sheet that swallowed the tea gardens. Varun, in the passenger seat, gripped the door handle out of habit.
Six months ago she had stalled on this exact slope four times while a jeep honked behind her. Today her feet did it without asking: clutch, a touch of gas, handbrake off. The car rolled up the hill and she let out a laugh.
'You're actually good at this now,' Varun said.
'I know,' she said, and grinned. Then, more quietly, 'Next I want to try the night drive down to Siliguri. And I still can't reverse into a tight spot. There's so much left.'
She said it without the old dread. The stalling months had got her here; the next ones would get her somewhere too. The wipers thumped steadily.

qa.q: How many times had Pema stalled on this slope six months ago?
qa.a: She had stalled on this exact slope four times.

qa.q: How can you tell Pema feels proud but also humble?
qa.a: She laughs and says 'I know' when praised, then quietly lists what she still can't do, like reversing into a tight spot 😊

qa.q: What would be a sensible next step for Pema as she aims for the night drive?
qa.a: She could practise reversing and driving with an experienced driver like Varun beside her before trying the night drive to Siliguri.

qa.q: What is it like for Varun to ride with Pema now?
qa.a: Varun still grips the handle out of habit, but he is impressed and can tell she is truly skilled now.

grounding: It shows a driver's pride after hard-won success, a hunger for the next challenge, humility about what remains, and trust that struggle pays off.
